## When consequences challenge the diagnostic relation

The [next continuation](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CALIBRATION-REVISION-INTEGRATION.md) now makes the previous full-load consequence available to the retained learner. A newly formed contact samples the persistent load and waste, with the issued command and context bound to that one-transfer history. It preserves the old weak report as historical evidence and stores the new indication separately. The original sensory model, earlier component completion and actual remaining support continue through the construction. Contact formation and fidelity remain declared local conditions.

An acquired failure can challenge a model’s use without immediately revealing which relation failed. Two actual parents have the same retained positive weak report and the same unsuccessful full operation. In one, the weak response was positive but did not predict the full effect; in the other, an earlier contact falsely reported a negative weak response as positive. The acquired full failure leaves eight physical alternatives. It changes the application judgment and activates a new weak test at the exercised setting through the independent contact. A fresh positive weak response exposes the local weak/full discrepancy; a fresh negative response contradicts the old report under the declared stable weak law. Both leave four alternatives, preserving what the evidence has not decided.

The acquired mismatch governs whether inquiry occurs. Both weak settings still distinguish candidates, so a supplied priority for the previously exercised setting determines the choice. A matched intervention retains the full evidence, revised application, proposal and their expenditure while disabling activation. An ordinary consumer of the same information matches the complete traces. Thus this result implements consequence-sensitive inquiry at the actual retained endpoint; it does not derive the origin or optimality of that inquiry policy.

Independent reconstruction accepts all 25 declared cases and 288 saved states, including unavailable or misleading observations and interrupted updates. No source is replenished and no second full operation occurs. One unit of delay leaves enough support to reach a correct local diagnosis but too little to retain the new interface. The full response represented concerns the preceding operation; fresh weak evidence alone does not establish a future full response. Formal verification of the new inference, resource and finite-correspondence claims is in progress.

The information limit is specific: models agreeing on the entire weak table and the tested full response can still disagree at the untested full setting. Repeating weak tests cannot resolve that difference. A new form of access or justified restriction could change the limit, while more support for the same weak tests alone would not. This connects improved understanding and its boundary within one activity, preserving the separate foundation questions concerning the formation of reliable access, inquiry rules and the significance of the undertaking.
